findings_fixed: RN1: long kit name wrapped the collapsed description to two lines and grew the card past the 188px floor, breaking the height-parity AC. Restored the repo's own guard from 304d3c77e (block min-w-0 truncate + title tooltip).
RN1: UniqueScansLeaderboard::toStat()'s docblock claimed the other two cards 'carry no such label' -- falsified by this change, corrected.

RN2 (HIGH): the blank-name fallback was a parallel PHP implementation of a documented query-layer guard, with a worse label (N/A vs the house 'Kit 1234') covering 1 of 4 render surfaces. Moved to the query layer at 3 select sites per KitScanPathsQuery:80 / ScanPlateStatsBatchQuery:274 / okf/concepts/scout-clickhouse-queries.md:47, and narrowed the PHP helper to truncation + escaping.
RN2: UniqueScansLeaderboard had ZERO PHPUnit assertions on the description whose rendering this change altered. Added coverage including an escaping test.
RN2: a test comment claimed the truncate assertion proved height behaviour it cannot prove; narrowed to what it actually pins.
RN2: the query guard is now tested where it lives -- a CH-free SQL assertion in CardQuerySqlFidelityTest, including that it wraps the AGGREGATE not the row.
findings_residual: Year-TTL caches defeat the blank-name guard on last_month and the 13-month chart history (3-lane convergence). today/last_7d/this_month -- the default view -- pick it up immediately. Real fix is cache-key versioning, shared by every CH query in the app.
RecoveryLeaderQuery keys its result map by kit NAME, so two same-named kits collapse and the card can headline the LOWER total. Pre-existing; the sibling query documents the opposite rule.
The clarity.kits join in RecoveryLeaderQuery has no FINAL; a mid-rename CDC row can appear twice and the new guard can render a plausible 'Kit 42' for a kit that has a real name. Needs-verification.
KitUserRecoveryLeaderboardQuery and KitUserRecoveries/LeaderboardTableWidget still render unguarded kit names on a leaderboard (different feature surface).
'Top Kit: N/A' on a swallowed ClickHouse failure reads as data. Pre-existing and systemic -- every card on the grid already renders 0 on that path.

rounds.note: RN1 PASSED the gate at 94 (arbitration; 3 Mediums, no High). The driver fixed the findings anyway because one of them broke a stated acceptance criterion (card height parity), and shipping a known AC break because the arithmetic rounded to 94 would defeat the point of the review. Code changed after a passing verdict, so RN1 no longer covers it. A scope round is not a fix cycle and does not consume the single gate-fix budget.

RN2 FAILED the gate: claude3 raised a HIGH (zero-tolerance floor) against leaderKitDescription()'s blank-name fallback -- code written by RN2's own scope-round fix, so this is a regression round, not a gate round, and it does not consume the single gate-fix budget. The finding was driver-verified and correct: the repo already documents a query-layer blank-kit-name guard (KitScanPathsQuery:80, ScanPlateStatsBatchQuery:274, okf/concepts/scout-clickhouse-queries.md:47) that yields an actionable 'Kit 1234'. The PHP helper was a parallel implementation with a worse label that covered 1 of 4 render surfaces. Fixed by moving the guard to the query layer per the convention.
